name: Microsoft Graph API Guidelines
description: Comprehensive style rules based on Microsoft Graph API Guidelines. Microsoft Graph provides a unified API endpoint for accessing Microsoft 365 services including users, groups, mail, calendar, files, and more. This profile includes Graph-specific patterns like OData conventions, navigation properties, actions, functions, and delta queries.
introduction:
Microsoft Graph is the gateway to data and intelligence in Microsoft 365. It provides a unified programmability model to access the tremendous amount of data in Microsoft 365, Windows, and Enterprise Mobility + Security.

This style specification formalizes the Microsoft Graph API design guidelines, which build on the Microsoft REST API Guidelines with additional patterns specific to the Graph API model.

principles.title: Unified Endpoint
principles.description: Microsoft Graph provides a single endpoint (graph.microsoft.com) for accessing all Microsoft 365 data and services.

principles.title: OData Compliance
principles.description: Microsoft Graph follows OData conventions for querying, filtering, and navigating resources.

principles.title: Incremental Synchronization
principles.description: Delta queries enable clients to efficiently synchronize local data with Microsoft Graph.

principles.title: Batch Request Support
principles.description: Batch requests allow clients to combine multiple operations into a single HTTP request.

categories.title: Permissions
categories.description: Scopes and consent for Graph API

patterns.name: Delta Query for Change Tracking
patterns.summary: Use delta queries to track changes to resources incrementally
patterns.problem: Clients need to synchronize local data with Microsoft Graph efficiently without fetching all data repeatedly.
patterns.solution: Use delta queries to get only changes since the last sync by calling the delta function and following deltaLinks.
patterns.when: When building applications that need to keep local data in sync with Graph

diagrams.title: Delta Query Flow
diagrams.content:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant G as Graph API
    C->>G: GET /users/delta
    G->>C: value + @odata.nextLink
    loop While nextLink exists
        C->>G: GET nextLink
        G->>C: value + @odata.nextLink
    end
    G->>C: value + @odata.deltaLink
    Note over C: Store deltaLink
    C->>G: GET deltaLink (later)
    G->>C: Only changed users

patterns.name: JSON Batching
patterns.summary: Combine multiple requests into a single HTTP call using JSON batching
patterns.problem: Making many individual requests to Graph API is inefficient and may hit throttling limits.
patterns.solution: Use the $batch endpoint to send multiple requests in a single HTTP call.
patterns.when: When an operation requires multiple Graph API calls

patterns.name: Change Notifications via Webhooks
patterns.summary: Subscribe to resource changes via webhooks instead of polling
patterns.problem: Polling for changes is inefficient and delayed.
patterns.solution: Create subscriptions to receive notifications when resources change.
patterns.when: When applications need real-time awareness of resource changes

glossary.definition: A resource with an identity (id property), such as user, message, or event.
A structured type without an identity, used as property values (e.g., emailAddress).
A property that links to related entities or collections.
A query pattern for tracking incremental changes to resources.
An opaque token representing a sync state for delta queries.
A URL containing a deltaToken, used to get changes since last sync.
A POST operation that may have side effects (e.g., sendMail).
A GET operation that returns data without side effects (e.g., delta).
The base URL for Microsoft Graph: https://graph.microsoft.com/{version}/
A webhook notification sent when a subscribed resource changes.
A way to add custom properties to Graph resources.
Untyped data that can be added to supported Graph resources.

rules.title: Use graph.microsoft.com endpoint
rules.rationale: Microsoft Graph provides a unified endpoint for all Microsoft 365 services.
rules.description:
All Microsoft Graph API calls should use https://graph.microsoft.com as the service root. The URL pattern is:

https://graph.microsoft.com/{version}/{resource}

judge.prompt: Check if the API uses the standard Microsoft Graph endpoint (graph.microsoft.com).

rules.title: Support /me alias
rules.rationale: The /me alias provides a convenient way for users to access their own resources.
rules.description: /me is an alias that refers to the signed-in user. It should be supported for all user-centric resources.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports the /me alias for accessing the signed-in user's resources.

rules.title: Use v1.0 for production, beta for preview
rules.rationale: v1.0 is the stable production version; beta is for preview features that may change.
rules.description:
Microsoft Graph uses two versions:
- v1.0: Stable, production-ready APIs
- beta: Preview APIs that may change without notice

rules.title: Support standard OData query parameters
rules.rationale: OData query parameters provide a standardized way to filter, sort, and shape data.
rules.description:
Microsoft Graph endpoints should support standard OData query parameters:
- $select: Choose which properties to return
- $filter: Filter results
- $orderby: Sort results
- $top: Limit number of results
- $skip: Skip results for pagination
- $expand: Include related resources
- $count: Include count of results

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents support for standard OData query parameters ($select, $filter, $orderby, $top, $expand).
passCriteria: Documentation mentions OData query parameter support
Query parameters follow OData naming conventions
partialCriteria: Some OData parameters are supported but not all
Custom query parameters are used instead of standard OData
failCriteria: No query parameter support is documented

rules.title: Use OData filter syntax
rules.rationale: Consistent filter syntax makes APIs more predictable.
rules.description:
Filter expressions should follow OData syntax:
- Comparison: eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le
- Logical: and, or, not
- Functions: startswith, endswith, contains

judge.prompt: Check if $filter uses OData syntax (eq, ne, gt, lt, and, or, startswith, contains, etc.).

rules.title: Support $expand for navigation properties
rules.rationale: $expand reduces the number of requests needed to fetch related data.
rules.description: Navigation properties should support $expand to include related entities in the response.

judge.prompt: Check if $expand is supported for including related resources in responses.

rules.title: Support nested $expand
rules.rationale: Nested expand allows fetching deeper relationships in one request.

judge.prompt: Check if nested $expand with query options is supported (e.g., $expand=members($select=id)).

rules.title: Document filterable properties
rules.rationale: Not all properties may be filterable; documentation should be clear about limitations.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents which properties support filtering and which filter operations they support.

rules.title: Define navigation properties for relationships
rules.rationale: Navigation properties express relationships between entities and enable traversal.
rules.description: Relationships between entities should be expressed as navigation properties. For example, a user's manager is accessed via /users/{id}/manager.

judge.prompt: Check if relationships between entities are expressed as navigation properties in the URL path.

rules.title: Support direct navigation to related entities
rules.rationale: Clients should be able to navigate directly to related resources.

judge.prompt: Check if navigation properties can be accessed directly (GET /users/{id}/manager) without needing $expand.

rules.title: Use $ref for relationship management
rules.rationale: $ref allows adding and removing relationships without modifying the entities themselves.
rules.description:
Relationships can be managed using $ref:
- POST /groups/{id}/members/$ref to add a member
- DELETE /groups/{id}/members/{userId}/$ref to remove a member

judge.prompt: Check if $ref is supported for managing relationships (adding/removing members, etc.).

rules.title: Use POST for actions with side effects
rules.rationale: Actions that modify state or have side effects must use POST.
rules.description:
OData actions are operations that may have side effects. They use POST and the action name appears in the URL path.

Examples:
- POST /me/sendMail
- POST /users/{id}/assignLicense

judge.prompt: Check if custom operations that modify state use POST method (OData actions).

rules.title: Use GET for functions without side effects
rules.rationale: Functions that only return data should use GET for cacheability.
rules.description:
OData functions are read-only operations that return data. They use GET and the function name with parameters in the URL.

Examples:
- GET /me/drive/root/delta
- GET /users/{id}/reminderView(startDateTime='...',endDateTime='...')

judge.prompt: Check if read-only operations that don't modify state use GET (OData functions).

rules.title: Namespace custom actions
rules.rationale: Namespacing prevents collisions and clarifies that an operation is custom.
rules.description: Custom actions and functions should be prefixed with a namespace like 'microsoft.graph.'

judge.prompt: Check if custom actions use namespace prefixes (e.g., microsoft.graph.*).

rules.title: Support delta queries for collections
rules.rationale: Delta queries enable efficient incremental synchronization.
rules.description: Collections that clients may want to sync should support the delta function. This returns changes since the last sync rather than all data.

judge.prompt: Check if key collections support delta queries for change tracking.
passCriteria: Delta function is documented for major collections
Changed and deleted items are clearly indicated
partialCriteria: Delta is supported but only for some collections

rules.title: Include @odata.deltaLink in final response
rules.rationale: The deltaLink allows clients to resume sync from where they left off.
rules.description: When all changes have been returned, the response must include @odata.deltaLink. Clients store this link and use it for the next sync.

judge.prompt: Check if delta query responses include @odata.deltaLink when no more pages remain.

rules.title: Indicate deleted items in delta
rules.rationale: Clients need to know which items were deleted to update their local state.
rules.description: Deleted items in delta responses should include @removed annotation.

judge.prompt: Check if deleted items in delta responses are indicated with @removed annotation.

rules.title: Support JSON batching
rules.rationale: Batch requests reduce HTTP overhead and help avoid throttling.
rules.description: The $batch endpoint allows combining multiple requests into a single HTTP call. Requests are sent as a JSON array and responses are returned in the same order.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports JSON batching via /$batch endpoint.

rules.title: Support request dependencies in batch
rules.rationale: Dependencies allow one request to use the result of another in the same batch.
rules.description: Batch requests can specify dependencies using 'dependsOn' to sequence operations.

judge.prompt: Check if batch requests support dependsOn for request dependencies.

rules.title: Limit batch size
rules.rationale: Large batches may time out or fail; smaller batches are more reliable.
rules.description: Batch requests should be limited to 20 requests per batch (Microsoft Graph limit).

judge.prompt: Check if documentation mentions batch size limits.

rules.title: Document required permissions
rules.rationale: Clear permission documentation helps developers request appropriate consent.
rules.description: Each API endpoint must document the permissions (scopes) required to call it. Microsoft Graph uses a permission model with delegated (user) and application permissions.

judge.prompt: Check if each endpoint documents required permissions/scopes for access.
passCriteria: Required permissions are documented for each endpoint
Both delegated and application permissions are listed
partialCriteria: Permissions are documented but not for all endpoints
Only one permission type is documented

rules.title: Support both delegated and application permissions
rules.rationale: Different scenarios require different permission types.
rules.description:
APIs should support:
- Delegated permissions: For apps acting on behalf of a user
- Application permissions: For daemon/background apps

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports both delegated and application permission types.

rules.title: Follow least-privilege principle
rules.rationale: Apps should request only the permissions they need.

judge.prompt: Check if the API offers granular permissions that follow the least-privilege principle.

rules.title: Return 429 for throttling
rules.rationale: 429 is the standard HTTP status for rate limiting.
rules.description: When a client exceeds rate limits, return 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents 429 Too Many Requests response for throttling.

rules.title: Include Retry-After header
rules.rationale: Retry-After tells clients when to retry after being throttled.

judge.prompt: Check if 429 responses include Retry-After header.

rules.title: Document rate limits
rules.rationale: Knowing rate limits helps developers design efficient applications.

judge.prompt: Check if rate limiting policies and limits are documented.

rules.title: Support schema extensions
rules.rationale: Schema extensions allow adding typed custom properties to Graph resources.
rules.description: Schema extensions provide a way to add custom properties with defined types to Graph resources.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports schema extensions for custom properties.

rules.title: Support open extensions
rules.rationale: Open extensions allow adding untyped custom data to resources.
rules.description: Open extensions provide a way to add custom key-value data to supported resources without defining a schema.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports open extensions for untyped custom data.

rules.title: Support change notifications
rules.rationale: Webhooks enable real-time notifications without polling.
rules.description: Applications can subscribe to receive notifications when resources change. Subscriptions are created via POST /subscriptions.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports webhook subscriptions for change notifications.

rules.title: Validate webhook endpoint
rules.rationale: Endpoint validation prevents subscribing to endpoints that don't exist or aren't controlled by the subscriber.
rules.description: When creating a subscription, the notificationUrl must be validated by sending a validation token that the endpoint must echo back.

judge.prompt: Check if webhook subscription creation includes endpoint validation via validation token.

rules.title: Support subscription renewal
rules.rationale: Subscriptions have expiration times and must be renewed to continue receiving notifications.
rules.description: Subscriptions should support renewal via PATCH to extend expirationDateTime.

judge.prompt: Check if subscriptions can be renewed before expiration.

rules.title: Use camelCase for property names
rules.rationale: Consistent naming improves API usability.
rules.description: All property names in Microsoft Graph use camelCase (e.g., displayName, userPrincipalName).

rules.title: Use DateTime suffix for timestamps
rules.rationale: Consistent timestamp naming clarifies data types.
rules.description: Timestamp properties should use the DateTime suffix (e.g., createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime).

judge.prompt: Check if timestamp properties use the DateTime suffix convention.

rules.title: Use consistent relationship names
rules.rationale: Consistent relationship names make navigation predictable.
rules.description:
Common relationships should use standard names:
- members: Collection of users/devices in a group
- owners: Collection of users who own a resource
- manager: Single navigation property to a user's manager

judge.prompt: Check if relationship navigation properties use standard Graph naming (members, owners, manager, etc.).

rules.title: Define entity types with id property
rules.rationale: Entity types have identities and can be addressed directly.
rules.description: Entity types must have an 'id' property that uniquely identifies the instance.

judge.prompt: Check if entity types include an 'id' property for unique identification.

rules.title: Use complex types for embedded data
rules.rationale: Complex types represent structured data that doesn't need its own identity.
rules.description: Structured data that doesn't need to be addressed independently should be modeled as complex types (e.g., emailAddress, physicalAddress).

judge.prompt: Check if embedded structured data uses complex types without id properties.

rules.title: Include @odata.type for polymorphism
rules.rationale: @odata.type enables type discrimination for polymorphic responses.
rules.description: When returning polymorphic data (e.g., directory objects that could be users or groups), include @odata.type to indicate the actual type.

judge.prompt: Check if polymorphic responses include @odata.type for type discrimination.

rules.title: Use enums for fixed value sets
rules.rationale: Enums document and validate allowed values.
rules.description: Properties with a fixed set of values should use enum types.

judge.prompt: Check if properties with fixed value sets use enum definitions.

rules.title: Include @odata.context in responses
rules.rationale: @odata.context provides metadata URL for the response.

judge.prompt: Check if responses include @odata.context for metadata reference.

rules.title: Include @odata.id for entities
rules.rationale: @odata.id provides the canonical URL for an entity.

judge.prompt: Check if entity responses include @odata.id with the canonical URL.

rules.title: Use standard Graph error format
rules.rationale: Consistent error format enables programmatic error handling.
rules.description: Error responses must follow Graph error format with error.code, error.message, and optionally error.innerError.

judge.prompt: Check if error responses use standard Graph error format with code and message.

rules.title: Include request-id in errors
rules.rationale: Request IDs enable support to trace and debug errors.
rules.description: Error responses should include request-id in innerError for troubleshooting.

judge.prompt: Check if error responses include request-id for tracing.

rules.title: Include date in error innerError
rules.rationale: Timestamp helps correlate errors with logs.

judge.prompt: Check if innerError includes date/timestamp.

rules.title: Support $search query parameter
rules.rationale: Full-text search improves resource discovery.
rules.description: Collections should support $search for full-text search across searchable properties.

judge.prompt: Check if $search is supported for full-text search.

rules.title: Document searchable properties
rules.rationale: Not all properties may be searchable.

judge.prompt: Check if searchable properties are documented.

rules.title: Support $count query parameter
rules.rationale: $count provides total item count for UI pagination.
rules.description: Support $count=true to include @odata.count in response.

judge.prompt: Check if $count=true is supported for collection counts.

rules.title: Include ConsistencyLevel for count
rules.rationale: Advanced queries may require eventual consistency mode.
rules.description: Some $count queries require ConsistencyLevel: eventual header.

judge.prompt: Check if ConsistencyLevel header requirement is documented for advanced queries.

rules.title: Support both v1.0 and beta versions
rules.rationale: Beta allows early access to new features while v1.0 ensures stability.

judge.prompt: Check if both v1.0 and beta versions are documented.

rules.title: Document beta limitations
rules.rationale: Beta APIs may change without notice.
rules.description: Beta version documentation should clearly state that APIs may change and should not be used in production.

judge.prompt: Check if beta API limitations are documented.

rules.title: Mark deprecated features in beta
rules.rationale: Deprecated features help developers plan migrations.

judge.prompt: Check if deprecated features are marked in the API documentation.

rules.title: Use @odata.nextLink for pagination
rules.rationale: Server-driven pagination using nextLink is the Graph standard.
rules.description: Collection responses with more results must include @odata.nextLink for pagination.

judge.prompt: Check if collections use @odata.nextLink for pagination.

rules.title: Support $top for page size
rules.rationale: Clients may need to control page size for performance.
rules.description: Support $top parameter to limit results per page.

judge.prompt: Check if $top parameter is supported for page size control.

rules.title: Document maximum page size
rules.rationale: Clients need to know page size limits.

judge.prompt: Check if maximum page size is documented.

rules.title: Support $skipToken for efficient pagination
rules.rationale: $skipToken is more efficient than $skip for large datasets.

judge.prompt: Check if $skipToken is used for efficient server-side pagination.

rules.title: Support advanced filter operators
rules.rationale: Advanced filters enable complex queries.
rules.description: Support advanced filter operators: any, all for collections; lambda expressions.

judge.prompt: Check if advanced filter operators (any, all) are supported.

rules.title: Document filter operator support
rules.rationale: Not all properties support all filter operators.

judge.prompt: Check if supported filter operators are documented per property.

rules.title: Use 202 Accepted for long-running operations
rules.rationale: LROs should not block the client.
rules.description: Operations that take more than a few seconds should return 202 Accepted with a status monitor URL.

judge.prompt: Check if long-running operations return 202 Accepted.

rules.title: Include Location header for LRO
rules.rationale: Location header provides the status monitoring URL.

judge.prompt: Check if 202 responses include Location header for status polling.

rules.title: Include percentComplete in status
rules.rationale: Progress indication improves user experience.

judge.prompt: Check if LRO status includes percentComplete for progress.

rules.title: Support client-state for webhooks
rules.rationale: Client-state helps verify notification origin.
rules.description: Webhook subscriptions should support clientState property that is echoed in notifications.

judge.prompt: Check if webhook subscriptions support clientState for verification.

rules.title: Include resource data in notifications
rules.rationale: Rich notifications reduce follow-up API calls.
rules.description: Support includeResourceData to include changed data in notifications (requires encryption).

judge.prompt: Check if rich notifications with resource data are supported.

rules.title: Support atomic batch operations
rules.rationale: Atomic batches ensure all-or-nothing semantics.
rules.description: Support atomicityGroup for transactional batch operations.

judge.prompt: Check if atomic batch operations are supported via atomicityGroup.

rules.title: Limit batch to 20 requests
rules.rationale: Graph limits batch size to 20 requests.

judge.prompt: Check if batch size limit (20 requests) is documented.

rules.title: Support incremental consent
rules.rationale: Incremental consent improves user experience by requesting permissions as needed.

judge.prompt: Check if incremental consent patterns are documented.

rules.title: Document admin consent requirements
rules.rationale: Some permissions require admin consent.

judge.prompt: Check if permissions requiring admin consent are clearly marked.

rules.title: Support streaming for large content
rules.rationale: Streaming enables handling large files without memory issues.
rules.description: Large content (files, attachments) should support streaming via $value endpoint.

judge.prompt: Check if large content supports streaming download.

rules.title: Support resumable upload
rules.rationale: Resumable uploads handle large files and network interruptions.
rules.description: Large file uploads should support resumable upload sessions.

judge.prompt: Check if resumable upload is supported for large files.

rules.title: Support Prefer header options
rules.rationale: Prefer header allows client preferences for response behavior.
rules.description: Support Prefer header options like return=minimal, odata.maxpagesize.

judge.prompt: Check if Prefer header is supported for response preferences.

rules.title: Support Immutable-Id for mailbox items
rules.rationale: Immutable IDs persist even when items move between folders.
rules.description: Support Prefer: IdType="ImmutableId" for stable mailbox item identifiers.

judge.prompt: Check if immutable IDs are supported for mailbox items.

rules.title: Support standard SDK patterns
rules.rationale: SDK-friendly APIs improve developer experience.
rules.description: API design should work well with Microsoft Graph SDKs for various languages.

judge.prompt: Check if the API follows patterns compatible with Graph SDKs.

rules.title: Support multi-tenant access
rules.rationale: Multi-tenant apps need cross-tenant data access.

judge.prompt: Check if multi-tenant application patterns are documented.

rules.title: Include service endpoint in documentation
rules.rationale: Service endpoint must be clearly documented.
rules.description: Documentation must include the Graph service endpoint: https://graph.microsoft.com

judge.prompt: Check if the Graph service endpoint is documented.

rules.title: Document national cloud endpoints
rules.rationale: Some customers use national/sovereign clouds.
rules.description: Document alternative endpoints for national clouds (US Gov, China, Germany).

judge.prompt: Check if national cloud endpoints are documented.

rules.title: Support ETags for concurrency
rules.rationale: ETags prevent lost updates in concurrent modification scenarios.
rules.description: Resources that can be updated should support ETags and If-Match headers.

judge.prompt: Check if updatable resources support ETags for optimistic concurrency.

rules.title: Return 412 for ETag mismatch
rules.rationale: 412 indicates the resource was modified since last fetch.

judge.prompt: Check if 412 Precondition Failed is documented for ETag mismatches.

rules.title: Document workload-specific limits
rules.rationale: Different workloads have different rate limits.
rules.description: Document specific rate limits for workloads like Outlook, OneDrive, Teams, etc.

judge.prompt: Check if workload-specific rate limits are documented.

rules.title: Document retry strategies
rules.rationale: Proper retry strategies prevent amplifying service issues.
rules.description: Document recommended retry strategies with exponential backoff.

judge.prompt: Check if retry strategies are documented.

rules.title: Support $value for binary content
rules.rationale: $value provides direct access to binary content.
rules.description: Binary properties (photos, content) should be accessible via $value suffix.

judge.prompt: Check if binary content is accessible via $value.

rules.title: Support $format query parameter
rules.rationale: $format allows requesting specific response formats.

judge.prompt: Check if $format parameter is supported for format selection.

rules.title: Use singletons for unique resources
rules.rationale: Singletons represent unique instances like /me or /organization.
rules.description: Unique resources should be modeled as OData singletons.

judge.prompt: Check if unique resources are modeled as singletons.

rules.title: Support derived type filtering
rules.rationale: Filtering by type enables querying specific entity types in polymorphic collections.
rules.description: Support filtering by derived type: /directoryObjects/microsoft.graph.user

judge.prompt: Check if filtering by derived type is supported.

rules.title: Support type casting in paths
rules.rationale: Type casting allows accessing type-specific properties.

judge.prompt: Check if OData type casting is supported in URL paths.
